tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1322) — Compare the entire narrow panicle with Yellow Indiangrass. The Flora describes a looser head with fewer flowers, usually 15–30 cm long.

Slender Indiangrass candidate: seek a loose, usually one-sided, arching flowering panicle on a dense warm-season perennial tuft. Two archived S. elliottii source-labelled photographs show curved awned heads but DO NOT independently prove species identity, crown architecture, or awn dimensions. Never identify by golden/brown color or an arch alone.
tiles.short: Arching, mostly one-sided panicle; confirm rooted tuft and long twice-bent awns
tiles.status: PROVISIONAL SOURCE-ID HOLD — REQUIRES VOUCHERED ANATOMY

tiles.heading: 02 · TRACE THE ROOTSTOCK
tiles.details: Inspect a connected mature plant from roots through flowering stem. The published southeastern key separates caespitose S. elliottii (no extended rhizomes) from rhizomatous S. nutans. A detached seedhead cannot establish rootstock type. No existing S. elliottii photo verifies an intact rooted crown, and an eastern record does not prove Hays County nativity.
tiles.short: Dense tuft without spreading rhizomes; contrast S. nutans

tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE REAL COLLAR
tiles.details: Pull the blade away from its sheath on a vouchered S. elliottii stem and show the true free ligule margin and any lateral extensions with a 1-mm scale. Panel 3 depicts the collar of OTHER SPECIES S. nutans, not S. elliottii; it must never be used as direct proof of this taxon's ligule. No unsupported ligule-length cutoff is asserted.
tiles.short: Photograph the inner ligule membrane at 1-mm scale

tiles.heading: 04 · ISOLATE THE FERTILE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Published World Flora Online treatment reports S. elliottii spikelets about 5–7 mm long. At 10–20× photograph one intact sessile fertile spikelet with an adjacent reduced/naked sterile pedicel; then separate and label glumes and lemma, measuring each rather than inferring glume venation or length from the whole head. Panel 4 is S. nutans reproductive anatomy for COMPARISON ONLY.
tiles.short: Spikelet body about 5–7 mm; check bare sterile pedicel

tiles.heading: 05 · MEASURE THE COMPLETE LEMMA AWN
tiles.details:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1320) — Trace the awn all the way from the lemma to its tip. The Flora key describes it as mostly 23–35 mm long, usually with two bends.

The cited World Flora Online account describes mature awns about 20–35 mm, twice bent and twisted below the second bend; a regional Florida key gives typically 25–40 mm (sometimes shorter). S. nutans is commonly shorter and once bent, but ranges overlap. Measure at least three complete awns from lemma attachment to tip with a millimeter ruler; separately record body length and both bend locations. The existing two source-labelled head photos cannot certify these measurements or the lemma attachment.
tiles.short: Usually 20–35 mm, twice bent and twisted below the second bend

tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT YELLOW INDIANGRASS
tiles.details: S. nutans usually has rhizomes, a fuller often golden panicle, and shorter commonly once-bent awns; S. elliottii is described as caespitose with an arching often one-sided head and longer twice-bent awns. Color, curvature, and any one awn are not conclusive. Panels 3–4 are explicitly S. nutans, not new S. elliottii evidence. Keep species identity and project-county status unresolved until independently authenticated specimen evidence is available.
tiles.short: Compare rootstock, one-sided head and several measured mature awns together
tiles.status: PROVISIONAL — SPECIES-ID AND RANGE HOLDS REMAIN

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: SLENDER INDIANGRASS candidate: archived two source-labelled AWNED very CURVED heads provide good candidate recognition. Strongest published mature split from S. nutans is dense NON-RHIZOMATOUS base, mainly ONE-SIDED ARCHING panicle, and typically 25–40 mm often TWICE-bent awns vs S. nutans rhizomatous, commonly once-bent 2–15 mm awns. Measure a true awn with mm ruler and verify actual base; the images do not prove these measurements. East Texas native is not automatic Hays County nativity. Species-level and county-range HOLD preserved.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: BEGIN gallery panel 8 index7 (Anne Parker, CC BY): real *S. elliottii* source species intact spikelets and their long attached awns immediately beside actual metal millimeter marks. Hairy spikelet outer surfaces seen, but the mature fertile lemma and each glume are NOT peeled apart.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Pull the blade away from its sheath on a vouchered S. elliottii stem and show the true free ligule margin and any lateral extensions with a 1-mm scale. Panel 3 depicts the collar of OTHER SPECIES S. nutans, not S. elliottii; it must never be used as direct proof of this taxon's ligule. No unsupported ligule-length cutoff is asserted.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Published World Flora Online treatment reports S. elliottii spikelets about 5–7 mm long. At 10–20× photograph one intact sessile fertile spikelet with an adjacent reduced/naked sterile pedicel; then separate and label glumes and lemma, measuring each rather than inferring glume venation or length from the whole head. Panel 4 is S. nutans reproductive anatomy for COMPARISON ONLY.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Compared with yellow Indiangrass S. nutans, this source-labelled grass often has longer (~1–1½ inch) awns and looser more strongly arching heads and tends to be nonrhizomatous; S. nutans generally has a denser straight/golden panicle, shorter (~⅓–1 inch) awns and short rhizomes. Root/collar/spikelet details overlap and must be checked on mature vouchered material. Local native status of S. elliottii remains UNRESOLVED.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.caption: Source CC0 photograph from South Carolina shows a live upright reddish grass culm and green-brown folded sheath with narrow leaves, with other grasses in the background. This is aboveground vegetative morphology only: no continuous exposed rooted crown or rhizome/no-rhizome diagnosis may be claimed from this image.

intro: SLENDER INDIANGRASS candidate: archived two source-labelled AWNED very CURVED heads provide good candidate recognition. Strongest published mature split from S. nutans is dense NON-RHIZOMATOUS base, mainly ONE-SIDED ARCHING panicle, and typically 25–40 mm often TWICE-bent awns vs S. nutans rhizomatous, commonly once-bent 2–15 mm awns. Measure a true awn with mm ruler and verify actual base; the images do not prove these measurements. East Texas native is not automatic Hays County nativity. Species-level and county-range HOLD preserved.
memory_rule: SLENDER INDIANGRASS CANDIDATE: warm-season perennial clump with an OPEN, ARCHING and relatively sparse panicle, usually 4–14 inches in mature southeastern treatments, with awned spikelets. Mature awns often 1–1½ inches, longer than typical yellow Indiangrass S. nutans (~⅓–1 inch), but color and arching alone overlap. Verify mature awn with mm/ruler scale, Sorghastrum fertile SESSILE spikelet plus NAKED sterile pedicel, and actual collar and perennial nonrhizomatous crown. Two genuine source-labelled photographs show awned CURVING heads, not those micro features. PROJECT TARGET-ZONE RANGE REMAINS UNRESOLVED; source determination needs independent voucher-level review.
safety_note: 9 physically archived species SOURCE-labelled real CC photos (7 new, 2 previous), 2 other-species comparator panels, 10 normal gallery panels after one photo held for morphology QC. New 13 gross pointers on actual photograph structures. Flora/research taxon and Hays county range hold remains. No rooted photo or full glume dissection, photo roles provisional 3.5/6=58%.
field_rule: A long bent awn and arching seedhead can suggest *Sorghastrum elliottii*, but they do not individually prove a Hays County occurrence. Confirm with exposed rootstock, true membrane ligule and attached mature spikelet/glumes at scale and a reliable specimen identity.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
comparison_text: Compared with yellow Indiangrass S. nutans, this source-labelled grass often has longer (~1–1½ inch) awns and looser more strongly arching heads and tends to be nonrhizomatous; S. nutans generally has a denser straight/golden panicle, shorter (~⅓–1 inch) awns and short rhizomes. Root/collar/spikelet details overlap and must be checked on mature vouchered material. Local native status of S. elliottii remains UNRESOLVED.
